title: Packet capture: reading the wire
summary: Capture traffic on a router with tcpdump and read a conversation layer by layer: ports, the TCP handshake, and HTTP.

nodes.router: you work here: all traffic between the two networks passes through it
nodes.workstation: runs a sync tool that polls the server, 10.13.1.10

tasks.title: Find the conversation
tasks.text: The **workstation** talks to the server `10.13.2.10` every few seconds. Capture on the **router** and find the TCP **port** on the server it connects to.
hints: `tcpdump -ni any host 10.13.2.10` shows every packet to or from the server. Wait a few seconds.
Lines look like `10.13.1.10.51234 > 10.13.2.10.NNNN`. The number after the last dot of the destination is the server port.

answer_cmd.cmd: timeout 12 tcpdump -lni any -c 4 'tcp and dst host 10.13.2.10' 2>/dev/null | grep -o '> 10\.13\.2\.10\.[0-9]*' | head -1 | awk -F. '{print $NF}'

tasks.title: The three-way handshake
tasks.text: Every TCP connection opens with three packets. tcpdump shows their flags in square brackets. What flags does the **second** packet (the server's reply) carry? Answer as tcpdump writes them, for example `[P.]`.
hints: Capture only connection openings: `tcpdump -ni any 'tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0'`.
`S` is SYN and `.` is ACK. The client sends SYN, the server answers with SYN plus ACK.

solution.note: Client sends `[S]` (SYN), server answers `[S.]` (SYN-ACK), client finishes with `[.]` (ACK).

tasks.title: Read the request
tasks.text: Plain HTTP is readable on the wire. Print packet contents as text and find the **User-Agent** the sync tool sends.
hints: `-A` prints each packet's payload as ASCII. Try `tcpdump -ni any -A port <the port from t1>`.
Look for a line starting with `User-Agent:` in the GET request.

answer_cmd.cmd: timeout 12 tcpdump -lni any -A -c 20 'tcp and dst host 10.13.2.10 and dst port {{PORT}}' 2>/dev/null | grep -a -m1 '^User-Agent:' | sed 's/^User-Agent: //; s/\r$//'

tasks.title: Read the response
tasks.text: The server's reply is just as readable. Capture it and submit the **reference** value it contains.
hints: Capture traffic coming **from** the server: `tcpdump -ni any -A src host 10.13.2.10`.
The body has a line `reference: DOJO{...}`.

answer_cmd.cmd: timeout 12 tcpdump -lni any -A -c 30 'tcp and src host 10.13.2.10' 2>/dev/null | grep -a -o -m1 'DOJO{[^}]*}'

tasks.title: Save a capture
tasks.text: Analysts save captures to study later or open in Wireshark. On the **router**, write at least 10 packets of this traffic to `/root/sync.pcap`.

checks.fail_msg: /root/sync.pcap is missing or has fewer than 10 packets.

hints: `-w file` writes raw packets instead of printing them. `-c N` stops after N packets.
`tcpdump -ni any -c 20 -w /root/sync.pcap port <port>`, then read it back with `tcpdump -nr /root/sync.pcap`.

steps.cmd: timeout 30 tcpdump -ni any -c 20 -w /root/sync.pcap 'tcp and host 10.13.2.10' 2>/dev/null; true
